newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DALY OPENS UP TWO-SHOT LEAD DURING SECOND ROUND OF PGA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DALY OPENS UP TWO-SHOT LEAD DURING SECOND ROUND OF PGA.

text.p: John Daly, continuing his spectacular play, leapfrogged past Davis Love to grab a two-shot lead during Friday's second round of the PGA Championship at Winged Foot.

Daly, a recovering alcoholic looking to redeem himself from the ignominy of quitting the U.S. Open in June with a bad case of the shakes, chipped in for birdie from just off the green at the par-3 seventh hole.
Love, 33, took a double bogey at the 16th for a three-shot swing at the top of the leaderboard.

The flip-flop left Daly, who missed the Masters and British Open after undergoing treatment for his illness, at five under par and dropped Love, who temporarily took the lead with a birdie at the par-4 15th, to three-under for the tournament.

Italian Costantino Rocca birdied the last two holes for his second successive 69 and a two-under 138 total, a figure matched by Jeff Maggert (69), Phil Blackmar (68) and Japanese 27-year- old Shigeki Maruyama (70).
In the clubhouse another shot back at one-under 139 were Greg Norman and Paul Stankowski.

Norman, who lost an 18-hole playoff at Winged Foot to Fuzzy Zoeller at the 1984 U.S. Open, had taken his score as low as three under par on the front nine before slipping back to post a 71 to follow his opening 68.
Tiger Woods improved by a shot, Justin Leonard stayed the same and Ernie Els dropped a stroke in the early holes of the dream threesomes' second tour of Winged Foot.
Masters champion Woods charged out with a pair of birdies on the first holes but gave a shot back with a bogey at the par-3 third hole to stand at one under.

British Open winner Leonard parred the first three holes to remain two under, while U.S. Open champion Ernie Els, the third member of the threesome uniting the season's major championship winners, bogeyed the second hole to stand at one over par.
Daly, 31, and Love began the day tied for the lead after both posted record-tying opening rounds of four-under 66.
Love, teeing off among the earliest starters, went on something of a roller-coaster ride in a round that included four birdies, three bogeys and a double-bogey.
The last birdie put him temporarily into the lead but the double-bogey dumped him out.
Love said a bad mistake in judgement -- when he elected to hit a 1-iron out of the rough from 225 yards away instead of chipping out -- led to his double at the par-4 16th.
"It was just a bad decision," admitted Love. "It cost me at least a stroke.
"If I had chipped out, nine out of 10 times I would have been able to put a wedge close enough to make par."
Instead, Love put himself into more trouble short of the green, then found a greenside bunker, blasted out strong and needed two putts to get down.
"I feel I can recover from a bad shot. I just don't need to make bad decsions," said Love, who led in the clubhouse at three-under 137 after his 71.
